content:
Requirement R16 (input): Expose ISR Sensor Data. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to request exposure of ISR sensor data..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-16.1, F-16.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-16.<F>.1, Be-16.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-16.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Let the pilot request exposure (display/output) of the UAV's ISR sensor data — bringing the sensor feed into the pilot's awareness.

**Function candidates:**

**F-16.1 — Summon ISR sensor feed into view.** Goal: the pilot obtains access to the ISR sensor data output (make it present/visible on demand). The teleology is *availability* — the data exists, the function is to expose it to the pilot.

**F-16.2 — Select which ISR data stream to expose.** Goal: the pilot chooses *among* multiple ISR sources/sensors what to bring up. Distinct from F-16.1 because the goal is discrimination/selection, not mere summoning — relevant if a UAV carries multiple sensors (EO/IR, radar, etc.).

**F-16.3 — Configure the exposed feed's presentation.** Goal: the pilot governs *how* the feed is rendered (layout slot, size, overlay vs. tiled). Teleology is arrangement of the pilot's visual workspace.

**Recommendation:** F-16.1 is the direct reading of R16 ("request exposure of ISR sensor data"). The use case (6.1) is a simple request→inform loop with no mention of multiple streams or presentation control. F-16.2 and F-16.3 are plausible extensions but read into the requirement more than it states — I'd log them as spin-offs unless you want a multi-sensor UAV assumption baked in now.

Note: F-16.1 pairs naturally with R13's status panel and R14's sensor-aiming — the "expose feed" surface is likely a **shared** structure with the ISR monitoring context, not exclusive to R16. Flagging for the Structure layer.

Which Function do you want to close on?

Closing on **F-16.1** (summon ISR sensor feed into view) and **F-16.2** (select which ISR data stream to expose). Both retained as distinct Functions.

Moving to **Behaviour**. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. I'll give pathways per Function.

---

**F-16.1 — Summon ISR feed**

**Be-16.1.1 (Touch-only):** Pilot taps a persistent "ISR FEED" affordance on the WAD → feed panel instantiates into view. One-shot summon. Re-tap dismisses (reuses R12 visibility-toggle logic).

**Be-16.1.2 (Keyboard-only):** Dedicated bezel OSS (or UCP soft-key) toggles the ISR feed panel on/off. Same one-shot semantics via discrete button.

No Mixed pathway adds value here — summon is a single atomic act; both paths already do the whole task.

---

**F-16.2 — Select which stream to expose**

**Be-16.2.1 (Touch-only):** Feed panel carries a source selector (tab strip or list of sensor sources, e.g. EO / IR / radar). Pilot taps a source → panel switches to that stream. Direct selection.

**Be-16.2.2 (Keyboard-only):** Bezel rotary steps through the available sources (detent per source), or UCP up/down keys cycle the active stream; current selection shown on panel. Stepping selection.

**Be-16.2.3 (Mixed):** Only worth it if source count is large — Touch to open the source list, Keyboard rotary to scroll/confirm. I'd **drop this** — with a handful of sensors both single-modality paths are complete and faster; Mixed adds no real value.

---

**Recommendation:** Be-16.1.1 + Be-16.1.2 for summon (both modality-complete, mirror R12). Be-16.2.1 + Be-16.2.2 for selection (both modality-complete). Skip Mixed.

Note: Be-16.1's summon toggle is essentially the same interaction as R12's status-panel visibility toggle — strong **shared-Behaviour** candidate. And the F-16.2 selector only exists once the panel is open, so it lives *inside* the F-16.1 panel structurally.

Agree on the four Behaviours, or want the Mixed path reconsidered?

About the 16.1
The ISR FEED can be a Panel/Window on the WAD and also a button on the UAV screen

I agree with the note on the four behaviorus plus this observation I said it

Noted. **Be-16.1.1 (Touch)** summon affordance is surfaced in two places:
- a dedicated **"ISR FEED" button on the UAV screen** (invocation from the UAV context), and
- the resulting **ISR Feed Panel/Window on the WAD** (which itself carries a header control to dismiss/re-summon).

This mirrors the multi-surface invocation pattern from R09/R14 (control offered across shared surfaces, not locked to one).

**Behaviour layer closed:**
- **Be-16.1.1** (Touch): one-shot summon/dismiss via UAV-screen button + WAD panel header control
- **Be-16.1.2** (Keyboard): bezel OSS / UCP soft-key toggle for feed panel
- **Be-16.2.1** (Touch): direct source selection via in-panel source tabs/list
- **Be-16.2.2** (Keyboard): rotary/UCP stepping through sources

Both F-16.1 paths modality-complete; both F-16.2 paths modality-complete. Mixed dropped.

---

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI element sets (reusing existing surfaces).

**S-16.1.1.1 — ISR Feed Panel + multi-surface invocation** (serves Be-16.1.1 & Be-16.1.2)
- **ISR Feed Panel/Window** on WAD (new stacked overlay layer, up to the 8-source limit) rendering the sensor stream — reuses R12/R13 Detail/Status Panel chassis (header, close X, persistent toggle).
- **"ISR FEED" button on the UAV screen** (Touch) — invocation entry point.
- **WAD panel header X / re-summon control** (Touch).
- **Bezel OSS or UCP soft-key** (Keyboard) — toggle equivalent.

**S-16.2.1.1 — In-panel source selector** (serves Be-16.2.1 & Be-16.2.2)
- **Source tab strip / list** inside the ISR Feed Panel (Touch) — one entry per sensor source (EO/IR/radar/…), active source highlighted.
- **Bezel rotary (detented) or UCP up/down keys** (Keyboard) — steps active source; selection reflected on the same tab strip.

This is a single structural build — the F-16.2 selector lives inside the F-16.1 panel, both Functions served by one panel chassis with shared invocation and shared source-control widgets.

**Shared-structure flags:**
- Panel chassis = **reuse of R12/R13** Detail/Status Panel (header, toggle, close).
- Toggle/notification behaviour ties into **R08** stack if you want summon acknowledgment.
- UAV-screen button pattern = same invocation logic as **R09/R14**.

Want an alternative structure set (e.g. HUD-slaved feed strip, or feed tiled vs. stacked), or does this single reuse-heavy build close it?

**Requirement R16 — closed.**

**Functions:**
- **F-16.1** — Summon ISR sensor feed into view
- **F-16.2** — Select which ISR data stream to expose

**Behaviours:**
- **Be-16.1.1** (Touch) — one-shot summon/dismiss via UAV-screen button + WAD panel header control
- **Be-16.1.2** (Keyboard) — bezel OSS / UCP soft-key toggle
- **Be-16.2.1** (Touch) — direct source selection via in-panel tabs/list
- **Be-16.2.2** (Keyboard) — rotary/UCP stepping through sources
- All modality-complete; Mixed dropped.

**Structure:**
- **S-16.1.1.1** — ISR Feed Panel/Window (WAD stacked overlay, reusing R12/R13 panel chassis) + "ISR FEED" button on UAV screen + WAD header X/re-summon + bezel OSS/UCP toggle
- **S-16.2.1.1** — in-panel source tab strip/list (Touch) + bezel rotary/UCP step keys (Keyboard)

**Reuse flags:** panel chassis ← R12/R13; multi-surface invocation ← R09/R14; optional summon-ack ← R08.

**Summary line:** R16 exposes UAV ISR sensor data via a reusable WAD feed panel — summoned/dismissed from a UAV-screen button or bezel/UCP toggle, with an in-panel source selector (touch tabs or keyboard stepping) to pick among sensor streams.
